questionText:
Which one of the following predicate formulae is NOT logically valid?

Note that $W$ is a predicate formula without any free occurrence of $x$.
explanation:
Step 1: Understand quantifier movement rules when $W$ contains no free occurrences of $x$.

Recall the logical equivalence for implication: $A ightarrow B \equiv eg A \lor B$.

Step 2: Evaluate Option (C):
LHS = $ orall x (p(x) ightarrow W)$
$\equiv orall x ( eg p(x) \lor W)$

Since $W$ has no free occurrences of $x$, the universal quantifier distributes over $ eg p(x)$:
$\equiv ( orall x eg p(x)) \lor W$
$\equiv eg (\exists x p(x)) \lor W$
$\equiv \exists x p(x) ightarrow W$

Hence, $ orall x (p(x) ightarrow W)$ is equivalent to $\exists x p(x) ightarrow W$, NOT $ orall x p(x) ightarrow W$. Thus, option (C) is NOT logically valid.

Step 3: Verification of Option (D):
$\exists x (p(x) ightarrow W) \equiv \exists x ( eg p(x) \lor W) \equiv (\exists x eg p(x)) \lor W \equiv eg ( orall x p(x)) \lor W \equiv orall x p(x) ightarrow W$, which is logically valid.
